A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACM-FD, with matching authors, core equations and retained experimental results. The complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original prediction and generation experiments on Darcy Flow, Convection Diffusion and Torus Fluid, including numerical results in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds diffusion-reaction predictions, function completion, uncertainty calibration and component ablations, reported throughout Tables 1–8.

M1.justification: The GP diffusion, masked zero-target loss and FNO denoiser are retained. Algorithm 2 corrects the sampling-noise multiplier from beta_hat_t to sqrt(beta_hat_t). The described GP-interpolation route for irregular inputs is omitted; the combined pointwise and whole-function masking strategy is newly documented within the existing flexible-mask framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds PDEBench diffusion-reaction data with four prediction mappings and half-domain function completion on Darcy Flow and Convection Diffusion. Conversely, v1's irregularly sampled prediction and generation scenarios disappear. Regular-grid coverage of the original three systems remains.

E2.justification: v2 adds an adapted Simformer for prediction and calibration, unconditional MFD for generation and ablations, and MFD-Inpaint plus interpolation for completion. The original operator baselines and beta-VAE remain in the retained comparisons; PODDON is relocated to Appendix Table 5 rather than removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include observing one domain half and completing the other, evaluating empirical coverage at three confidence levels across eight tasks, and timing computation with and without Kronecker structure. Runtime comparisons aggregate neural-operator training across tasks. The original 1,000/100/200 training/validation/test split and 64-by-64 regular grids are retained.

E4.justification: v1 has no component ablation suite. v2 Appendix D tests removing random masking, varying masking probability around 0.5, and removing Kronecker computation, with results in Tables 6–8. Figures 2 and 6 also add prediction-error/uncertainty and completion case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report prediction means and standard deviations over five training runs. v2 additionally constructs 90%, 95% and 99% predictive intervals from 100 samples, evaluates their empirical coverage, and displays predictive standard deviations in Section 5.4. This substantially expands uncertainty assessment without establishing an increase in training-run counts.

E6.justification: Original regular-grid prediction values are unchanged in v2 Tables 1 and 5, and regular generation scores are retained in Table 2. v2 adds diffusion-reaction, new-baseline, completion, calibration and ablation/runtime results while removing irregular-sampling results. For example, the new diffusion-reaction f1,u1-to-f2 task reports errors of 0.0144 for ACM-FD and 0.0107 for FNO.

T1.justification: Algorithm 2 replaces beta_hat_t times epsilon with sqrt(beta_hat_t) times epsilon, correcting the sampling variance to match Equation 8. The principal diffusion derivations and Kronecker complexity analysis otherwise remain, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The single-model arbitrary-conditioning claim remains, but the stated contributions change substantially. v2 removes irregular-data handling from the abstract and contribution list, claims stabilization through zero regularization, and adds comparative claims about completion accuracy, uncertainty calibration and generation quality comparable to unconditional diffusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking zero-target regularization to stability and conditional training to completion quality. It interprets MFD comparisons as preserving unconditional generation quality and discusses masking sensitivity. Appendix D also qualifies efficiency claims: cheap epochs do not eliminate the larger training budget or higher total training time than FNO and DON.

D1.justification: v2 provides an ACM-FD code-release link and documents the summed pointwise/whole-function masking losses, Simformer's DDPM and linear-attention adaptations, its tuning ranges, diffusion-reaction data preparation, and A100 hardware and training/runtime details. v1's irregular-data sampling and interpolation instructions are removed.

R1.justification: Section 4 replaces much of the general generative-model survey with focused discussion of functional diffusion and conditional inference. Added predecessors include Kerrigan et al. (2023), Lim et al. (2023), Franzese et al. (2024) and Gloeckler et al. (2024). v2 acknowledges conceptual similarity to prior GP-based diffusion and distinguishes Simformer through zero regularization.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution discussion, related-work section and experimental narrative are substantially reworked. Qualitative generation discussion moves from the main text into Appendix C, while experiments gain separate completion, calibration and ablation sections. Much of the core mathematical exposition remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one-column to two-column layout. v2 adds a method schematic, uncertainty and completion visualizations, and several analysis tables. The original generation comparison is expanded with MFD and moved to Figure 3; v1 Figure 2 survives as Figure 4. PODDON results are split into an appendix table.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's missing validation of completion, predictive uncertainty and individual design choices through Tables 3–4 and 6–8. Relevant diffusion comparators, clearer prior-work positioning and additional reproducibility information strengthen the evidence. Irregular-sampling validation is lost, and Section 5.1 overstates superiority over GNOT relative to Table 1, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial improvement in support for the central claims.
